01

Project introduction

A threat profile of one ransomware sample, written as a cyber threat intelligence exercise for a simulated client, NorthByte Cybersecurity Ltd. The sample is a 32-bit Windows DLL that 54 of 62 antivirus engines on VirusTotal label as DarkSide.

The profile answers three questions a SOC needs answered: what is this file, what does it do, and what should we do about it. It ends with indicators, ATT&CK mappings, a detection rule and six prioritised actions.

Training exercise, draft statusThis is a draft (v1.0, for peer review) written on public-source intelligence. The original carries a TLP:AMBER marking, and this page is a summary. Several items in the original are still marked to complete, and they are listed under Limitations rather than hidden.

03

Key judgements

Confirmeddirectly supported by sample dataRecoveredartefact recovered from the evidencePotentialpresent but not shown to be user-initiatedInterpretationanalytical readingHypothesisworking idea, untestedLimitationconstraint on what can be claimed
  • ConfirmedThe sample is DarkSide ransomware (High confidence). 54 of 62 detections, vendor labels that agree on the family, five independent YARA rules, and sandbox runs that show ransom notes and renamed files.
  • InterpretationThe brand is defunct but the model continues (Moderate confidence). The sample was compiled on 5 April 2021 and first seen on 1 May 2021. DarkSide closed in May 2021, and its operators are linked to BlackMatter and then ALPHV/BlackCat.
  • InterpretationOverall confidence is Moderate. Detection and sandbox data are strong. Static analysis is limited to VirusTotal metadata, and some checks are still outstanding.
04

History and lineage

DateEvent
August 2020DarkSide first spotted
November 2020Ransomware-as-a-service model launched
March 2021DarkSide v2.0 released
5 April 2021Compile timestamp of the assigned sample
7 May 2021Colonial Pipeline attack; FBI later attributes it to DarkSide
May 2021DarkSide announces it is shutting down
31 July 2021BlackMatter appears, assessed as DarkSide returning
November 2021BlackMatter shuts down
April 2022FBI advisory links BlackCat to DarkSide and BlackMatter

DarkSide is sold as a service: operators build the ransomware and affiliates carry out the intrusions, so attribution depends on the affiliate. The operator group is tracked as GOLD WATERFALL by Sophos, and Mandiant tracks affiliate clusters UNC2465, UNC2628 and UNC2659. A claim that FIN7 operated DarkSide could not be corroborated, so it is not reported as attribution.

05

Attack lifecycle

Reported initial access routes include spearphishing links, password spraying against VPN, and exploitation of exposed services. Operators have used PowerShell, Certutil and Bitsadmin to fetch the ransomware and PsExec and RDP to spread it. Stolen data went to Tor leak sites and file-sharing services.

06

Static analysis

The file is a small DLL with two non-standard sections and two sections whose entropy points to encrypted content. It statically imports a single function, so the rest of its behaviour is hidden until run time.

SectionEntropyObservation
.text6.09Main code, below 7.0
.text15.13Non-standard name; probably holds the entry point
.rdata3.22Very small read-only data
.data7.71Likely packed or encrypted data
.ndata7.94Non-standard name, highest entropy
  • RecoveredOne static import. DisableThreadLibraryCalls only. Sandbox data shows the other APIs resolved at run time.
  • InterpretationPacking is inferred, not named. VirusTotal did not name a packer. The evidence is indirect: entropy, section names, the single import and a ClamAV label of Packed.
  • LimitationNo signature data. VirusTotal returned none, so the file is treated as unsigned with Moderate confidence.
07

Behaviour in sandbox runs

  • ConfirmedExecution via rundll32.exe with the DLL as the target.
  • RecoveredRansom note and renamed files. A README.[8-hex ID].TXT note and files renamed with an 8-hex suffix; the ID changes per run.
  • RecoveredEnvironment checks. Disk, debugger, OS version and processor count were queried before encryption.
  • PotentialLong sleeps were tagged, which may be time-based evasion.
  • LimitationNo persistence mechanism seen. Registry writes were ordinary WMI entries, not Run keys.
  • LimitationMutex and registry names are not used for detection, because they matched Windows or sandbox noise.

The two C2 domains come from Emerging Threats rules on TLS server names. The third was contacted in a sandbox run but is not corroborated. Fifteen sandbox IP addresses were not assessed, because many look like shared cloud infrastructure and need enrichment before any blocking.

10

Detection

No verified strings were available, because the sample was not downloaded and the metadata gives no readable strings from a packed file. Guessing strings from other DarkSide samples would risk false positives, so the rule matches structure instead.

YARA rule DarkSide_OU
import "hash"
import "pe"
import "math"
rule DarkSide_OU {
  meta:
    description = "DarkSide ransomware x86 DLL: exact SHA-256, or structural fingerprint"
    date = "2026-11-20"
  condition:
    hash.sha256(0, filesize) == "156335b95ba216456f1ac0894b7b9d6ad95404ac7df447940f21646ca0090673" or
    ( uint16(0) == 0x5A4D and pe.is_dll() and pe.machine == pe.MACHINE_I386 and
      pe.imphash() == "6c8408bb5d7d5a5b75b9314f94e68763" and
      for any s in pe.sections : ( s.name == ".text1" ) and
      for any s in pe.sections : ( s.name == ".ndata" and math.entropy(s.raw_data_offset, s.raw_data_size) > 7.5 ) )
}

LimitationThe rule has not yet been tested. The test run against a clean file and a positive control is still to be done.

11

Recommendations

#ActionCategory
1Block baroquetees[.]com and rumahsia[.]com at DNS, proxy and firewall, and retro-hunt logsPrevent
2Deploy the YARA rule plus the Elastic and McAfee ATR DarkSide rules to EDRDetect
3Hunt for rundll32.exe loading DLLs from Temp or ProgramData, README.*.TXT files and mass renames to an 8-hex extensionDetect
4Isolate and reimage confirmed hits, restore from offline backups, and check for data theft before restoringRespond
5MFA and password-spray detection on VPN, patching of internet-facing systems, restricted RDPPrevent
6Train staff to spot phishing linksPrevent

Limitations and open items

  • LimitationDraft status. Version 1.0, awaiting peer review. The reviewer is not yet named.
  • LimitationMISP search results are still to be added.
  • LimitationMalwareBazaar record and family tag are still to be checked.
  • LimitationYARA test results are not yet recorded.
  • LimitationRecent reporting. The newest source found is from April 2022, and a check for 2025 to 2026 reporting is still to be done.
  • LimitationStatic analysis rests on VirusTotal metadata. The sample itself was not downloaded or detonated by the analyst.

14

Final takeaway

A good threat profile says what is known, what is reported and what is still open.

The sample is clearly DarkSide. What the profile adds is a split between what this file shows and what the wider campaign is reported to do, with confidence stated at each step and the unfinished work listed.
